utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in this courtroom. Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning everyone in the courtroom. This is case number IT-06-90-T, The Prosecutor versus Ante Gotovina et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Mr. Tchernetsky, before you'll be further cross-examined, I would like to remind you that you are still bound by the solemn declaration that you have given at the beginning you have your testimony; that is, that you will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. Mr. Kehoe, are you ready to cross-examine Mr. Tchernetsky.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tchernetsky, Mr. Kehoe is counsel for Mr. Gotovina. Please proceed, Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Tchernetsky.

utterances.speaker: ALEXANDER TCHERNETSKY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. Tchernetsky, I would like to cover a couple of topics, several topics that were covered not only during your direct examination, but also that were covered in your witness statements.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And if we could begin the discussion with the Cetina period -- area, and I'd like to bring up on the map 1D23-0035, if I could.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. Tchernetsky, this is an original map, a working map from the latter part of July of 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honours, obviously, it has Croatian on it. I have taken the liberty of designating some of the Croatian translations in English; and, for ease of reading, Your Honours, I can likewise show you that as well, which is 1D23-0036. What I've taken the liberty of doing here, Your Honours, is if you could see the individual boxes that are in the -- starting with the upper left-hand corner, where it says: "Work map, start 25 July 1995, end 30 July." This is not -- this is a map which is a working map. The blue line is a line which was, in fact, the confrontation line. The red line is where the HV forces wanted to be in -- on the July 30th, 1995. So, if you see over in the right-hand corner, we have some other designations which notes "defence military secrets, summer 1995." And if we can just down a bit, it says: "Commander Major-General Gotovina Ante Gotovina." If we move over to the left, it shows, just a bit, the Croatian command post. And, Your Honour, I have also circled - if we with could move up just a bit, Mr. Monkhouse -- the town of Knin, the of Strmica, and the town Bosansko Grahovo. Those are the overlays -- the additions to the original map that you were made; but, suffice it to say, we will discussing this map over the course of both the Cetina issues, Your Honours, as well as the Strmica issues that were addressed by the witness yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, if we could just -- taking a look at this particular map, Mr. Tchernetsky, if we can look at the bottom left-hand portion near the confrontation lines. Mr. Tchernetsky, that area is basically the Cetina valley, is it not?

utterances.speaker: ALEXANDER TCHERNETSKY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see the Cetina valley here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And the particular designation there is an designation for the -- excuse me, the 1st Brigade of the North Dalmatia Corps of the army of the Republika Srpska which was in Vrlika. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ALEXANDER TCHERNETSKY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In Vrlika, there were military units of the RSK.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And how far was the -- Vrlika from the confrontation line that was designated here in blue?

utterances.speaker: ALEXANDER TCHERNETSKY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot recall exactly, but it was five to seven metres [as interpreted], as I far as I remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, if the witness says that he sees the Cetina valley, perhaps we could use the cursor, not to mark it, but at least that we have an idea what is on the mind of the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I will gladly have him mark it as a separate exhibit --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, I am not seek to have additional. But if the witness could at least tell us where he sees the Cetina valley, then I'm better able to follow his testimony.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's not very visible on the map. I cannot show you exactly because it doesn't show population centres, at least not that I can read it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You said you see Cetina valley. Could you, with the cursor mark, indicate approximately --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I suppose that this is Cetina valley, this valley, as far as I understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I can help the witness. Maybe, it might be easier, for the working purposes, if we move to D153. Now that we have this specific on this map, we can move to D153.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I am going to be moving and talking about these. But, at this time, if I can move into evidence the working map which is 1D23-0035, and then the map with our additions on it which is 1D23-0036.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No objections. Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the map, 1D23-0035, becomes Exhibit D219, and the map, 1D23-0036 becomes Exhibit D220.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, if we can blow up --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I think the first one, D119, that is the first one. No, let me just ...

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: That's the first one, Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's the working.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D219 is admitted into evidence, and then the second one, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the second map was the map with the red circles. It was 1D --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. It was the one that was marked D220. I take it no objections, then, Mr. Russo; therefore, it is also admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: In an answer above, the witness's answer was five to seven "kilometres," not "metres."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for the correction. Please proceed, Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, if we can just blow up the bottom portion of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Tchernetsky, if we look at the Cetina valley, is that an indication to you of the approximate area the Cetina valley that you discussed yesterday?

utterances.speaker: ALEXANDER TCHERNETSKY [Resumed]
utterances.text: If that is the territory that is marked by red here, then it's not. The Cetina valley, I'm showing now on the map, is what we called Cetina valley. It's this area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And it's in and around what you are pointing to as the village of Cetina. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ALEXANDER TCHERNETSKY [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's around the village and further to the south.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: ALEXANDER TCHERNETSKY [Resumed]
utterances.text: The valley, itself, is to the south of the population centre of Cetina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And you also mentioned yesterday the town of Kijevo. And how far is Kijevo from -- along that road, how far is Kijevo to Cetina?

utterances.speaker: ALEXANDER TCHERNETSKY [Resumed]
utterances.text: From Vrlika towards Knin, approximately halfway.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Could you give us an approximate kilometre distance from Kijevo to Cetina?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, we have a map with a scale.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: That's fine, Judge. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. Tchernetsky, we're going to move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I apologise for that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Tchernetsky, how many times -- before the Operation Harvest, how many times had you been to the Cetina valley area during -- from the time you got there in June of 1995 until Operation Storm on the 4th of August?

utterances.speaker: ALEXANDER TCHERNETSKY [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the Cetina valley, before the beginning of Operation Harvest, I was there at least three times; and in the course of that operation, at least two or three times again. So, in total, about six times within that month.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And during that period of time, sir, when you were there, the three times prior to Operation Harvest, were you driving through with other UNMOs?

utterances.speaker: ALEXANDER TCHERNETSKY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And, likewise, when you were there the two to three times during Operation Harvest, that was a week period of time. Correct?

utterances.speaker: ALEXANDER TCHERNETSKY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Operation Harvest lasted for seven or eight days in the end of August, just before Operation Storm.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, sir, you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I take it that there is a mistake with "end of July."

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Judge. That's right, end of July.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation]yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, sir, there were long stretches of time where you were not in the area. Is that right? You and the other UNMOs were not in the Cetina valley?

utterances.speaker: ALEXANDER TCHERNETSKY [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I'm personally am concerned, that's true. But this route was part of the constantly covered routes by our UNMOs, and that area was controlled on a permanent basis.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, if we can put this in a military context in July of 1995, during this period of time, General Gotovina and his troops were moving up the Dinara mountains and threatening the area of the Cetina valley and also Grahovo through a series of attacks, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: ALEXANDER TCHERNETSKY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I know that there are many ways of using artillery and mortars, one of such ways is to use had a harassing fire against the enemy in order to keep him under constant tension, to disorganise his work, and to force retaliation which would discover his deployment of forces. I believe that there, just as in Strmica, the Croatian side used precisely this way. However, in fierce violation, in blatant violation of prior agreements, this fire was used also against population centres, not only --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... my question was very -- my question was this: If we could put this in a military context of 1995, during this period of time, General Gotovina and his troops were moving up the Dinara mountains and threatening the area of the Cetina valley and also Grahovo through a series of attacks, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: ALEXANDER TCHERNETSKY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It was not General Gotovina who threatened the area. It's the Croatian army that used such ways as harassing fire that could cause retaliation from the certain side. That is one of the normal --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tchernetsky, the question was whether at that point in time, troops, as Mr. Kehoe said, under the command of Mr. Gotovina, whether they at that time were moving up the Dinara mountains. Could you first answer that question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I cannot know that because it was happening in a territory that was not controlled by our group, by our team.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- if it was happening.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That is a clear answer. You say, I do not know, I could not know. The second part of the question was whether, by this movements of troops, the area of Cetina valley and Grahovo were under attack. Do you know that? Can you confirm that? Do you have knowledge of that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know whether the Croatian army was under fire.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. The question is not whether -- whether they -- by moving, whether they attacked the forces --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as Grahovo is concerned, it was the territory of Bosnia. It was not within our mandate. We have never been there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed, Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, sir, you did a -- let's make this simplistic. You did a crater analysis in Cetina. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ALEXANDER TCHERNETSKY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And you made a determination that the firing had come from the area of Bosnia, right?

utterances.speaker: ALEXANDER TCHERNETSKY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. From the territory of Bosnia, from the direction of Bosnia --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: ALEXANDER TCHERNETSKY [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- from the Dinara mountains area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And if we look at the map on the screen, that is on the other side of the blue confrontation line, right?

utterances.speaker: ALEXANDER TCHERNETSKY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Fire was directed at this territory that I'm showing on the map, the area of Cetina, and it came from the mountain range.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, sir, the crater analysis that was done, were you called in to do that crater analysis by the army of the Republika Srpska Krajina?

utterances.speaker: ALEXANDER TCHERNETSKY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Our assignments came from the sector headquarters, along with the protests from the Serbian side.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, the protests came from the army of the Republika Srpska, didn't it?

utterances.speaker: ALEXANDER TCHERNETSKY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what kind of an authority, civilian or military, initiated these protests. I received my assignments from the commander of the UNMOs.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I made -- there was a -- I misspoke there, Your Honours. I meant to say that the protests came from the army of the Republika Srpska Krajina. Very different from the army of Republika Srpska. I do believe, based on the answer, Judge, that the answer would be the same because he just doesn't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm saying, once again, I don't know who made these protests, civilian or military authorities of the republic of Serbian Krajina. Our team received its assignments from the headquarters of the sector.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I understand, sir. Now, with regard to the actual crater analysis, you were obviously not there when that firing took place. Correct?

utterances.speaker: ALEXANDER TCHERNETSKY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct. We were not there during the firing. We were sent there to investigate the outcome.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And, sir, as a person that has been -- had a career in the military, you're familiar with the concept of mobile targets, aren't you?

utterances.speaker: ALEXANDER TCHERNETSKY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't quite understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, you are familiar with the concept of equipment moving, be it tanks or APCs. Those are pieces of military equipment that can move. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: ALEXANDER TCHERNETSKY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Naturally.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, since you were not there, you don't know if there was any type of APC or tank or other piece of military equipment belonging to the army of the Srpska Krajina in Cetina when the HV fired, causing the crater analysis that you analysed. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: ALEXANDER TCHERNETSKY [Resumed]
utterances.text: In those locations where we found -- where we found craters, there were no traces of movement of any machinery, and there were no traces of vehicles of such mobile units, as you are suggesting.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, you mentioned to us that you saw a MRL, a multi-barrel rocket launcher, in Kijevo yesterday. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: ALEXANDER TCHERNETSKY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And I can confirm that there was an anti-aircraft gun in position in Kijevo. I cannot remember the exact calibre, but it was 57 or 76 millimetres.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let us go to P -- excuse me, D86.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, sir, here's a photograph of an M-77 multi-barrel rocket launcher. Now, you mentioned to us yesterday, at page 3176 on line 17: "In the area of Kijevo, as far as I remember, we saw a piece of artillery, a rocket launcher in position. Now, was it a rocket launcher like this, sir?

utterances.speaker: ALEXANDER TCHERNETSKY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, but maybe it was misinterpreted. I'm going to look through the transcripts. I said yesterday, and I'm saying it again today, it was an anti-aircraft artillery piece, an anti-aircraft gun. It was either 57 or 76 millimetres in calibre. I cannot remember exactly. You are showing me, on this photographs, launchers of the kind that I have not seen.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I show them to you, sir, because you mentioned yesterday that you saw a rocket launcher in Kijevo. Now, did they have --

utterances.speaker: ALEXANDER TCHERNETSKY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was saying the same thing yesterday, that I saw an anti-aircraft gun. I was not talking about rocket launchers. I was talking about an anti-aircraft gun.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, there may have been a translation issue. There are ways of checking that, but the testimony of the witness, at this moment, appears that it was not a rocket launcher but an anti-aircraft weapon.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I'm operating from yesterday's transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm not blaming you, I'm trying to --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I understand, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, sir, did they have multi-barrel launchers, mobile rocket launchers, in the Cetina valley or in Vrlika or in Kijevo? Do you know?

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I can please ask him to maybe just take it one at a time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: That's fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do not mind here, as a matter of fact, because either the answer is, yes, there were, and then we can specify; or they were not, and then we have covered all three in one stroke. Please proceed, Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the course of my entire stay in the territory of Serbian Krajina, I did not see any rocket launchers during any of my missions in that territory.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, could one of the reasons that you didn't see them there was because you were not permitted to go into the military storages for the army of the Republic of Serb Krajina?

utterances.speaker: ALEXANDER TCHERNETSKY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot comment on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, if I may --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know what the Serbian side was guided by when it refused to allow us into the places where heavy weaponry was stored.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We have two questions, as a matter of fact, whether he was allowed; that's the first one. And the second is whether that could be a reason. I could answer that question. If it was not allowed, that could be a reason.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. Tchernetsky, you were not allowed to go into the Serbian military storages to check for heavy weapons, were you?

utterances.speaker: ALEXANDER TCHERNETSKY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Our team, at least during my tenure in that team, we were not allowed to go into military storage points that were in the territory covered by our team.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So, logically, you don't know -- were there military storage facilities in and around the Cetina valley area?

utterances.speaker: ALEXANDER TCHERNETSKY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I'm speaking about collection points that were organised in accordance with the agreement on cease-fire. Officially, these sites came under the jurisdiction of UNMOs. They were supposed to be under their control.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And where were those collection sites?

utterances.speaker: ALEXANDER TCHERNETSKY [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were two such collection sites in the Knin area, and one was - I can't remember the exact name of the settlement - but it was halfway on the road between Knin and Drnis, somewhere halfway through. In accordance with the mandate, they were under the control of observers; however, we were not given access to such sites. And in all such cases, protests were drawn up, and they were forwarded to the Serbian side by the sector headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Tchernetsky, let me ask you, going back to the Kijevo situation with the anti-aircraft gun, I mean, do you know what that anti-aircraft gun was firing at and what it was protecting?

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. There has been no testimony that that anti-aircraft gun was fired at anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think, logically, one can draw that if they have an anti-aircraft gun several kilometres away, that the question is where is it pointing and what is it firing at, I mean, if the line is five kilometres away at most?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You're giving the answer, more or less, Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, no, I am just explaining -- I'm answering the objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, as a matter of fact, you're not answering the objection. You could ask the witness whether he has seen it firing or whether he has any knowledge in what direction it was targeting. At the same time, I get the feeling that it takes us quite a while to make a point. If there were in the movable targets, that the witness might not have observed before he entered the area, where he did the crater analysis, that he might not have known about such a target at this moment. That appears -- if that is your point.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, I don't understand your question, Judge. I mean, there is a --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We started with the crater.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And, apparently, from the earlier answers of the witness, it appears that he has never seen any military target where he found a crater. And I think we are now spending quite a lot of time on the possibility that there may have been a moving target in that area. I mean, that point was clear to me already seven minutes ago. If that's the issue, ask the witness directly whether he knows anything about moving targets in the area. Because he said he didn't see any trace of that, that doesn't mean that it wasn't there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. That's all clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: That's fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So please come to your point, make your point, if it is the point. Of course, I never know what your point will be, but this came into my mind approximately seven minutes ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If I may, Judge, in response to that. That is true that he doesn't know if it was there, but the Prosecution put them on for this particular purpose to try to prove that there is an indiscriminate fire going into the Cetina valley, when this witness doesn't know --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's fine. But that was clear already seven minutes, as I said before. Yes. It's not the first time that we are in a courtroom, Mr. Kehoe, the, Judges, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I understand that, Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, taking this, sir, did you see where this anti-aircraft gun was pointed? I'm talking about the one in Kijevo.

utterances.speaker: ALEXANDER TCHERNETSKY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Anti-aircraft guns are intended for air targets, in the case of an air-raid, air attack, so they're not pointed anywhere. It's just that if there's -- if enemy appears in the air, these anti-aircraft guns are pointed at this enemy.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: One moment, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, with regard to the air attack, you noted that the anti-aircraft guns are intended for air attacks, in case of an air attack. Was there a weapons depot in Kijevo that the anti-aircraft gun was protecting?

utterances.speaker: ALEXANDER TCHERNETSKY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about any such depot.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Well, do you know what it was protecting?

utterances.speaker: ALEXANDER TCHERNETSKY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that such a depot existed in Kijevo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tchernetsky, the question now was whether you knew what it was protecting. You told us already that you were not aware of a weapons depot, but it could be other things that were protected, other facilities. Do you know what it was that this anti-aircraft gun protected?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I didn't know that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, sir, let me read to you -- you know Mr. Ermolaev, do you not? He was your --

utterances.speaker: ALEXANDER TCHERNETSKY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And reading from his transcript from 28 April 2008, page 2436, from line 15 through line 17: "Now just going back to the Cetina valley, there was a restriction of movement by the UNMOs in the Cetina valley in July of 1995. Correct? "Answer: 'Yeah, correct.'" So, in fact, sir, in July 1995, there was a restriction of movement on the UNMO, wasn't there?

utterances.speaker: ALEXANDER TCHERNETSKY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can neither confirm nor deny, because as far as I'm concerned, I was never subjected to any restriction of movement myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, sir, let me turn your attention to D154, page 7 of 21.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, if we go to blow up the top of that page and it notes that the subject of the meeting is: "The lifting of the restriction of movement. The security situation UNMO team, ARSK, official stated. UNMO teams should have freedom of movement in the area of the 1st Battalion of the North Dalmatia corps." That's in Vrlika, I think we established before. "But to secure their safety, there must be permission from the liaison officer in Knin." So, Mr. Tchernetsky, before you went into the area of the 1st Battalion of the North Dalmatia Corps which included the Cetina valley, you had to ask permission of the ARSK in Knin, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: ALEXANDER TCHERNETSKY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. As far as I remember, we went to Cetina without any hindrance. As for the check-points of the positions of the 1st Battalion of the Dalmatia Corps, we went to Vrlika on our way there and we would receive -- we would contact the liaison officer there. This was at the demarcation line or the line of confrontation. It was precisely there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. Tchernetsky, before an UNMO team went to the Cetina valley, this UNMO report indicates that they had to go to the liaison officer in Knin first to get permission. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. First of all, that is not what the report indicates; and, second of all, the witness has already testified several times that he never experienced any restriction of movement, and he did not have to ask for permission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: These are not the same questions, whether he experienced any hindrance when going to the area. Are you aware that before you went to the Cetina area, that permission was sought from the liaison officer in Knin? Are you aware of any such thing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honours. The procedure was as follows: When the inspection was made of Serbian positions at the confrontation line, we would normally receive permission from Serbian military authorities. When patrolling our regular routes, including the ones in the Cetina area, we did not seek any such permissions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. It depended on the purpose of your tour --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- whether permission was obtained. Please proceed, Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, sir, Mr. Ermolaev was your supervisor -- I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I didn't mean to cut off an answer, if there was an answer, Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you were about to say something, please do so.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. I don't want to add anything. Everything is fine as it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. Tchernetsky, when Mr. Ermolaev told this Court that there was a restriction of movement in the Cetina valley in July of 1995, would it be he or another supervisor among the UNMOs that would have been the person to go down and get permission from the liaison officer in Knin?

utterances.speaker: ALEXANDER TCHERNETSKY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I repeat, once again, that our team did not come across any obstacles when moving in the Cetina area. While conducting inspection of Serbian positions at the confrontation line, in accordance with the instructions from the headquarters, we had to inform the Serbian side about that, and we had to receive permission from the liaison officer. The Serbian positions were to the south, much more to the south, from the Cetina valley.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And when you got permission to go into the area of the 1st Brigade of the North Dalmatia Corps, before you got there, the army of the Republika Srpska Krajina knew that the UNMO team was coming, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Your Honour, the witness testified about permission to go to the confrontation line. Now we're broadening the area to the area of the -- of the 1st Brigade of the North Dalmatia Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I'm simply reading the situation report of what the ARSK officer said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's fine. But I think that we should, first of all, orient ourselves to what the witness said; and if you are quoting from some other source, then make it clear that you are quoting from a report, rather than repeating what the witness said.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So, Mr. Tchernetsky, when you were moving - and I'm reading from the report - in the area of the 1st Brigade of the North Dalmatia Corps, and you had secured the -- their permission from the LO in Knin, before you got there, the Krajina Serb army knew that you were coming, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Again, this does not reflect what we have in evidence. We have in evidence this line of this report, and we have the statement of the witness. Mr. Tchernetsky, if you just went for inspection, not visiting Serbian positions, would the - let me check exactly what - would the Krajina Serb army be aware of you going into that area? So I'm now talking about the normal inspection tours.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I've already spoke about that, Your Honour, and I will repeat. When conducting planned patrols, we did not inform about the direction of movement of our patrol teams. These plans changed periodically, and sometimes we visited the same site twice in a row. The Serbian side was not informed about that, not on a single occasion, except, as you have understood me correctly, except for the inspection of immediate combat positions of the Serbian troops at the confrontation line.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Even if on inspection tours you did not inform them, do you have any clue as to whether they knew even without being informed by you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't think so, because, let me say, once again. Our plans were periodically changed, and the order of touring certain regions changed periodically.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But they could be informed by check-points or in any other way, is that right, so apart from whether they knew of your plans?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I cannot know, Your Honours, how they controlled the movement of our patrols and our observers, so I cannot comment on that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes. I mean, throughout July, Mr. Tchernetsky, there was, in fact, a deterioration of the -- with the freedom of movement in the areas controlled by the North Dalmatia Corps. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: ALEXANDER TCHERNETSKY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No additional obstacles existed. I do not remember them. We patrolled our area in accordance with the plan, and I don't remember coming across any difficulties or hindrances in our movement. There was certain areas we were not allowed to enter. That's how it was in earlier July and in late July, and this situation was reported on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, again, Mr. Tchernetsky, Mr. Ermolaev, on page 2434, line 4: "Question: So, you would agree with me, Mr. Ermolaev, that in July, in order to move into the area of the 1st Brigade of the North Dalmatia Corps, you had to have the permission of the army of republic of Serb Krajina, didn't you? "Answer: Yes. But regarding July and answering yes, I mean we had general deterioration with the freedom of movement, I mean, in this side as well. Right, absolutely correct. Not only there, not only in this area." Now, Mr. Tchernetsky, do you disagree with the comments and testimony of Mr. Ermolaev?

utterances.speaker: ALEXANDER TCHERNETSKY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This confirms, once again, the first part that you read, that Mr. Ermolaev said that in order to visit the positions of the 1st Battalion, we had to obtain the permission from the Serbian military authorities. I said the same thing. When inspecting their positions, we needed to first go to the headquarters of the brigade and receive permission and escort by liaison officers of the Serbian army. But that was only if we inspected their positions. As for deterioration of the situation, when it comes to movement, I don't know. Mr. Ermolaev was in the headquarters of the sector. I can only testify about the area of responsibility where our group worked; and in that area, I do not remember that there was any deterioration in terms of the freedom of movement.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So, Mr. Ermolaev [sic], if the army of the republic of Serb Krajina had a tank in Cetina, you would have had to have the permission of the liaison officer in Knin to examine that, wouldn't you?

utterances.speaker: ALEXANDER TCHERNETSKY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so, because we had access to other areas, to other positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I will note that Mr. Ermolaev - and I won't belabour this, Judge - says the area of the 1st Brigade of the republic of Serb Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, in fact, sir, the --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let us turn to page -- excuse me. I apologise to the translators for coughing into the microphone. I'm sorry. D155 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: D155, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Tchernetsky, in fact -- excuse me. In fact, General Gotovina did order a cease-fire to allow the harvest to go forward, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: ALEXANDER TCHERNETSKY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Forgive me. This is the first time I see this document. Can I please go through it?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I apologise, sir. Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: ALEXANDER TCHERNETSKY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have read the document now. The only mistake that I see in it is that the work is conducted under the escort of the UNCRO patrols -- UNHCR, rather, UNHCR, and not under the civilian police of UN. Actually, the people worked under the protection of the UNMOs and under the protection of the civilian police of the UN.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: General Gotovina did allow the harvest to go forward and stopped firing, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: ALEXANDER TCHERNETSKY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In the presence of our monitors and in the presence of the monitors from civilian police, there was no firing.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let's turn to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tchernetsky, the question was whether Mr. Gotovina gave his permission for unhindered - now let me read it literally - did allow the harvest to go forward. Do you know anything about whether Mr. Gotovina took such a decision, apart from what you read on a document that you said you have never seen before?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't know anything about that earlier. I didn't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for that. May I take it that the answer that you just gave, is that based on what you saw in this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, the Chamber is not assisted by a witness reading a document, and then without any further factual basis to interpret whether it is true or not true what's in that document. I mean, we've seen that document, we have read that document. Now the witness has read the document as well. The only thing he could tell us, unless you establish a proper basis for anything else, is to read and interpret what the document says. That's as far as matters stand now. Of course, the witness has testified, and that's what he knows, is whether they were fired at or not. I mean, that is his personal knowledge, but this type of seeking confirmation of what is in a letter the witness has never seen before and that he has no knowledge whatsoever about who ordered and whatever, does not assist the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If I may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: The inference coming from the Prosecution case is, during the direct testimony, was that the firing stopped simply because UNCRO went there and -- or CIVPOL went out there and they were protecting the harvesters from doing that; when, in fact, from this document where General Gotovina meant with General Forand, which we have in Exhibit 157, he agreed to allow the harvesting to take place.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The document is in evidence, isn't it? It's just a question of what this witness could add to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: That is exactly right, Judge. What I am here to counter, Judge, is the inference from this witness that the only reason why they were there was to counter HV fire, and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I fully understand. At the same time, Mr. Kehoe, the Chamber does not expect a witness to have full knowledge of everything we know about. And if the witness, even if that would be an inference, I don't think that he is specifically said that this was not under instructions et cetera, he just observed what he saw. Now the witness has limited knowledge. That's clear. The Chamber has, in fact, far more knowledge. And I take that in the examination of Mr. Forand, we will find out more. We know this document. We are not in this courtroom to give such information to the witnesses that they are better able to make better inferences of what they have seen. We are here to listen to what the witness observed, and we'll put together with the assistance of the parties all the bits and pieces of the evidence, and whether this witness has finally a knowledge which allows him to make proper inferences, yes or no, is not something we should worry about too much. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, with regard to your work in the Cetina valley, Mr. Tchernetsky, you noted that you were with CIVPOL and you were taking turns in the fields, is that right? Did I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: ALEXANDER TCHERNETSKY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, you were there to ensure not only that the HV didn't fire but also that the ARSK didn't fire. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: ALEXANDER TCHERNETSKY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We were there only to demonstrate the UN flag, that would prevent the Croatian side from firing, because earlier that area was under fire only from the Croatian side.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, were you -- were you aware of the request by General Gotovina, prior to agreeing or prior to allowing the harvest to go forward, were you aware in any of your discussions at UNCRO or UN headquarters that, excuse me --

utterances.speaker: ALEXANDER TCHERNETSKY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me. What request are you talking about?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I'm not finished, sir. Were you aware of the request by General Gotovina or anybody from the HV staff that in order to agree to stop firing on to the Cetina valley, UNCRO had to control the ARSK firing positions from the Cetina valley? Were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: ALEXANDER TCHERNETSKY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew nothing about the existence of such an order. I saw it for the first time here in this courtroom; and that confirms, once again, that before that order, the area of Cetina valley was under fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: That doesn't exactly answer my question, Judge. I don't whether I want to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I leave it to you whether you want to insist on receiving an answer on the question. Of course, the witness said, but I don't know whether he was confusing, that he was not -- he knew nothing about such an order. Where he were talking about a request, I don't know whether that is any confusion about that. Then he started drawing conclusions, which are his conclusions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, quite simply, and without going into the particular exhibit were you aware that the HV was requesting UNCRO to control firing positions of the ARSK in the Cetina valley in order to allow the harvesting to go forward? Were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: ALEXANDER TCHERNETSKY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was not aware of that. But as I was within my team, I worked in the field, not in the headquarters, and any information about requests from the Croatian side is something I wouldn't know. I didn't know about.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I will just refer Your Honours to D157, page 2, and move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, sir, if we look for one more moment at D154 and go back to the page we were at, this is again the UN CIVPOL report of the 4th of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If we go to page 7 of 21, and just blow up that top portion.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And, again, we go to that next paragraph in there, and this is the ARSK official: "He also stated that the security situation was deteriorating do to HV reinforcements at the Dinara," and he gives grid references of it. If we go down two indentations: "Peace is only possible if UN establishes zone of separation, Krajina and Bosnia deployment of heavy weapons, 40 kilometres from the zone of separation." Were you aware, sir, that -- the first thing, were you aware that the HV had moved up the Dinara and was reinforcing their troops in the Dinara?

utterances.speaker: ALEXANDER TCHERNETSKY [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I was able to observe that, whether there were troops of the HV or HVO, I didn't know. But in the area of the Dinara mountains, we saw movements of heavy weaponry. I personally saw a tank, or maybe two, and I saw army personnel moving.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, sir, during your discussions at UNMO headquarters, were you aware that the army of the republic of Serb Krajina wanted to have both sides move weaponry 40 kilometres from the zone of separation?

utterances.speaker: ALEXANDER TCHERNETSKY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was not aware of that. I was not in the headquarters, and I didn't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. Tchernetsky, when you were at the headquarters and talking to the members of your team, did you discuss the possibility that the ARSK was complaining about HV activities and shelling because they were trying to buy time and they wanted the protection of the UN? Did you discuss that?

utterances.speaker: ALEXANDER TCHERNETSKY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: ALEXANDER TCHERNETSKY [Resumed]
utterances.text: At least, I did not participate in any such discussions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, let us move back, if we can, and we'll move ahead to a separate issue and that would be the Strmica issue, again in July.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And if we can move back to D220. It's probably the easiest one to work with.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, again, Mr. Tchernetsky, this map has the confrontation line of the 25th of July in blue and the area where the HV wanted to move lined in red, not all of which was successful, but just for the sake of looking at this particular map. Now, Strmica was on the road from Knin to Bosansko Grahovo and then on to Drvar, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: ALEXANDER TCHERNETSKY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And from the early part of July into -- well, let me -- did you know about HV advances up the Dinara towards Grahovo through the early part and up to mid-July of 1995?

utterances.speaker: ALEXANDER TCHERNETSKY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Officially, we were not informed about that, but there were rumours; although, the headquarters did not officially give us notice.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, you knew, sir, that the -- HV was threatening Grahovo, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: ALEXANDER TCHERNETSKY [Resumed]
utterances.text: At what time?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, throughout July of 1995, sir, going into the latter part of July.

utterances.speaker: ALEXANDER TCHERNETSKY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot tell you. I have never given it any thought. Was I aware of Grahovo or not? It was not in our area of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Tchernetsky, you do know that Grahovo fell to the HV on the 27th/28th of July, 1995, don't you?

utterances.speaker: ALEXANDER TCHERNETSKY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall precisely, but it's likely that this information did reach us. But I cannot remember clearly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. Tchernetsky, let's put this in context a little bit. Let me show you a video of 1D23-0001, a video from mid-June 1995 with Milan Martic speaking - excuse me - and in Grahovo, I'm reminded.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "We are not facing defeat, nor will we suffer defeat. I am convinced that we have the strength, quite enough strength to oppose our enemy who is not as strong as he would have us believe. They are united, the Muslims and the Croats, because the US and Germany demand this of them. But they are not stronger than us. I affirm that. I know this. I know that Serb fighters were always better and will be better. "Now, as well, we are aware of the situation and we have mobilised all forces in the Knin corps. And in all the corps of the Republika Srpska Krajina, there is a state of full readiness. This morning, we had a meeting to this effect, where we put everything into a state of full mobilisation and readiness. "We know that the loss of Grahovo is major, and this territory -- we know what this territory means. If we lose Grahovo in this territory, all of Krajina will be lost, and we are aware of that. And it is for this reason that I have come here to tell. I've come to tell you that Grahovo mustn't fall under any circumstances, and that not a single piece of Serb territory can fall "From this moment on, it is imperative to halt the Croatian Muslim aggression. We are sending reinforcements from all areas, from Knin, Bankovac, and all the parts of Republika Srpska. And the forces are already here, and be assured their aggression is being stopped. And at this time, even though it is risky to be telling you this, but I stand firmly behind this claim, the situation will change. "In order to accomplish all of this, we need to be fully disciplined. The need is so great that we have not tasked the command of corps with this task. It is instead under the command of both Main Staffs; that is, that the command of General Mladic and General Mrksic who are jointly launching this operation. "We no longer have any reason to hide from anyone the fact that we are joint defending ourselves. If the Muslims and the Croats can create a joint army, so can we. We shall demonstrate this through our actions. I tell you, we have our joint army and our joint strength. This is not a parade. But we shall demonstrate this through actions. "We have the right to this, too; and for this reason, we have the right as one nation to create a unified army and to create a unified state, and we are creating it and we have no shame. We are not ashamed of it. "I was told today by the highest international institutions that we mustn't create a joint state. I said we will, and there is no other option for us because the only way for us to survive is to create a joint state. And one of the basic preconditions for the creation of this joint state is our unified army, and we shall demonstrate this for the first time. You know that we have already demonstrated this in Bihac in penetrating the corridor. "And in all other areas, we fought together; but in this case, we no longer have any reason to hide from anyone. Whom should we be hiding from? Because we are fighting for our land and not for someone else's territory."

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. Tchernetsky. I was just waiting for the translation to come through.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, this video-clip from HVTV, 1D23-001, we will move into evidence at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Russo.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D221, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D221 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Tchernetsky, in order to supply the Bosansko Grahovo area through Knin, you have to travel up through Strmica, don't you?

utterances.speaker: ALEXANDER TCHERNETSKY [Resumed]
utterances.text: The main road, the most convenient road from Knin to Grahovo, goes through Strmica. That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let us put 1D23-0033 on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I could, just before the questioning starts about this exhibit, if this is something which is again pieced together from original documentation, we would ask for the provenance of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Clearly, Judge, based on the witness's testimony right now to supply Grahovo, he would move up the road that was going, as the witness just said, through Strmica into Grahovo. The item that we have noted there is Grahovo. It notes the date of 27/28 July 1995, which is the date that Grahovo fell.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Your Honour, that's not -- well, I was referring to the clear outlined arrows which indicate a thrust from the middle and two from the sides, and that seems to indicate to me troop movements. I'm wondering if that is something which is pulled from a contemporaneous map.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes. I mean, Your Honour, we will gladly provide the information supporting what the troop movements were of the various brigades under the command of General Gotovina when Bosansko Grahovo was attacked. There was, in fact, a flanking manoeuvre.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Does this give you sufficient information at this moment for us to proceed?

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, you noted for us during the course of your testimony, and I do believe you put it on a map of an area through Bosansko Grahovo, the road through this village that had been shelled prior to your getting there on the 30th of July. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ALEXANDER TCHERNETSKY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Either the 29th or the 30th, one of the last days of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, even prior to that time, you talked to us about shelling in the area of the town of Strmica. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ALEXANDER TCHERNETSKY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, if we look at this particular map, that area that you designated, if I may --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: That area that you designated is, in fact, the supply route that the ARSK used to take personnel and supplies from Knin through Strmica up into Grahovo. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: ALEXANDER TCHERNETSKY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot be the judge of that, because as to any massive movements of army troops or military equipment towards or out of Grahovo, I didn't see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, sir, part of the job of the UNMOs was to look to see what kind of movement was taking place among the RSK, wasn't it? Not just you, I'm talking about all the UNMOs.

utterances.speaker: ALEXANDER TCHERNETSKY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. Such movements were easiest to keep an eye on from Strmica, where they were positions of the Kenyan Battalion overlooking the road itself, and the command of the Kenyan Battalion regularly reported to the sector staff headquarters about any movements on that road.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, let turn your attention to P209.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Excuse me. At this time, Your Honour, I will tender the item that's on the screen right now, which is 1D23-0033.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Russo.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: No objection, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This becomes Exhibit D222, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D222 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now this is the map that you drew yesterday; and in the area of R2, that is the road that goes right up through Strmica up to Bosansko Grahovo, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: ALEXANDER TCHERNETSKY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And consistent with Mr. Martic's statements, if they were supplying Bosansko Grahovo through or from Knin or even Bankovac, they would drive up through this road into Bosansko Grahovo, wouldn't they?

utterances.speaker: ALEXANDER TCHERNETSKY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not informed of intentions of the Serbian side as to what route to use to supply, but it is quite likely that this is the shortest way to Grahovo and that it would be used.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, prior to the actual shelling taking place, you were getting complaints, or I think you noted for us -- and let me just back up for a second so I can just put this in context, in fairness to you. I'm looking at your testimony yesterday, on page 3180 at lines 10 and 11. Sir, it is your testimony yesterday. It is not in the statements, Mr. Tchernetsky.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Judge, I am just trying -- he is looking at the statements, and it is actually his testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tchernetsky, Mr. Kehoe will read from what you said yesterday, rather than the statement that was put on paper earlier. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now I don't have yet the Tuesday transcript with the full numbering of pages. I still have the daily numbering of pages.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Frankly, Judge, I'm not sure what that one is. I think it is 3180. Is that the final?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: For me, it goes from 1 to 86, and then usually there will be finalised and then get the sequential numbering. If you give me two or three words, then I will find it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: How about - let me see - let's say: "With cooperation ..."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Cooperation. I will find it. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I don't know cooperation, per se, with.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's yesterday's transcript page 9, line 23, apparently. That is where it says: "It was in the end of July we received an assignment from ..." That's the beginning of the answer, is that it?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, it is, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, just by way of clarification, is the 3180 not the official page?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It will be the official page. Usually, the pages are numbered on the day itself from starting at 1, and then they become part of the consolidated transcript, and then they get sequential numbering, where we start somewhere in 3.000. It might be that number. It usually comes during the day.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you give me the specific words, then it is easy to find. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Tchernetsky, you noted on line 10 to line 12, "This investigation ..." Talking about your trip to Strmica on the 30th: "This investigation was performed at the request of the ARSK command and with cooperation of the military units of the army of the RSK."

utterances.speaker: ALEXANDER TCHERNETSKY [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was on orders of the headquarters. We had the liaison officer of the 7th Corps of the ARSK with us.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, by the way, when you went into the Cetina -- you had a liaison officer from the ARSK that went up there to Strmica with you, you just said. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ALEXANDER TCHERNETSKY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Was that also true when you went into Cetina?

utterances.speaker: ALEXANDER TCHERNETSKY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was talking about Strmica, about the Strmica incident to Cetina. We went alone without any military from the RSK.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, going back to Strmica, you went to Strmica with a liaison officer because there were restriction of movement there, weren't there?

utterances.speaker: ALEXANDER TCHERNETSKY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The thing is that the command of the ARSK addressed the sector headquarters with a protest against the fire targeting Strmica; and in order to show us exactly where the targets were so that we wouldn't wonder about, they gave us this liaison officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Were there restrictions of movement on the UNMOs in the Strmica area?

utterances.speaker: ALEXANDER TCHERNETSKY [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Strmica, there was no restriction of movement.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let me turn no your attention, again, to Mr. Ermolaev's testimony on the 29th of April, 2008, page 2449, line 3 to line 5: "Question: So when it came to going to the Strmica area, there were restrictions of movement on the UNMOs? "Answer: Yes." Do you disagree with that, sir?

utterances.speaker: ALEXANDER TCHERNETSKY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I disagree with that. At least our team of UNMOs did not come across any such restriction in the area of Strmica. Let me say this, again. Strmica was an area where the Kenyan Battalion was located. We patrolled, they patrolled, and we visited them almost every day.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: But you did pick a liaison officer up before you went there from the northern barracks, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: ALEXANDER TCHERNETSKY [Resumed]
utterances.text: We picked up the liaison officer from the corps headquarters, so that he could show us specifically the places where shells hit so that we wouldn't search the entire territory.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, sir, isn't it a fact that when you got up into the Strmica area, you picked up another ARSK colonel who was there to show you where the impacts were? Isn't that a fact? So, in fact, two ARSK officers are with you.

utterances.speaker: ALEXANDER TCHERNETSKY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Your Honour, I --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. Just one, just one. One whom we picked up from the corps headquarters, and he escorted us to Strmica and took upon himself to show us the places that he were shelled.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Russo, is there still --

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I will withdraw that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So your testimony, Mr. Tchernetsky, is when you got up to the Strmica area, you did not pick up another ARSK officer to ride with you?

utterances.speaker: ALEXANDER TCHERNETSKY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We already had one officer with us. We didn't pick up anybody else. The liaison officer from the corps was already with us.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I notice it's 10.30. I don't know if you want to us to break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If this would be a suitable moment to take a break, we will. Yesterday, I think you indicated that you would need two hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Actually, I said at least two hours, Judge. I have a little bit going through this stuff, so that's probably --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You're urged to finish your cross-examination within the two-hours that you mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I will do my utmost to do that. There are many issues that were set forth in the 92 ter statements that need to be addressed, in addition to these two larger issues, and I will do it as quickly as possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe I do understand there are a lot of issues. As I said before, we look at what is presented as evidence in chief, we look at how cross-examination is conducted. I refer to my earlier observations about what we try to achieve and what does assist the Chamber and what does not assist the Chamber, and that it should not be our main concern whether the witness leaves this courtroom with full knowledge of what he has not observed and to draw the right inferences. Please keep that in mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will resume at 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, as far as the issue about multi-rocket launchers or anti-aircraft guns is concerned, I was informed by the interpreters that the terms used by this witness yesterday and today is the same. Apart from that, one of the Judges on this Bench understands Russian, and it is his recollection, although he admits not being a military expert, that the witness talked consistently about an anti-aircraft gun. Of course, it's still usually, if we want to correct the transcript or the translation, there's a formal procedure for that. I, however, suggest that, where you're still free to seek such a verification, that at least it's now put on the record that two sources have confirmed that the witness spoke about an anti-aircraft gun.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, I accept Judge Gwaunza's explanation because I know of her expertise in Russian.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Just kidding, Judge. Point of levity.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I feel a bit hurt by the fact that you consider not to be fluent in Russian. But if that is your position, Mr. Kehoe, I will accept it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, Judge, just know that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: At the same time, it is, I think, the moment to also express our gratitude to those who are translating into Russian. I follow channel 7 frequently in order to have the pleasure of listening to the Russian translation as well. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I was just reading from the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If I may, Mr. Tchernetsky --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If we can go to 65 ter 2518.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And, now, just highlighting the top portion the 27th of July, this is a letter from Lieutenant-General Mile Mrksic of the ARSK. In the first paragraph, Mr. Tchernetsky, it says: "For several days now, the Croatian army HV and the Croatian defence counsel have been constantly firing their artillery and tanks on the Drvar-Grahovo-Knin road without interruption. Operations was the most intense the 24th, 25th, 26th, and 27th of July."

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Before I move to the map, I would offer this item into evidence and I will begin to ask some questions about it as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Russo.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D223, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D223 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. If we could move our attention to D172.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, this is map previously received in evidence, Mr. Tchernetsky, that has circled Knin, Strmica, Grahovo, and Drvar. Now, if we go to the top, Drvar, at that time in July, was the headquarters of the 2nd Krajina Corps of the army of the Republika Srpska, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: ALEXANDER TCHERNETSKY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So you had no knowledge of where the -- the Bosnian Serb army's headquarters was. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ALEXANDER TCHERNETSKY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Are you familiar with the road in that the ARSK was supplying Bosansko Grahovo from Drvar down into Grahovo in July of 1995?

utterances.speaker: ALEXANDER TCHERNETSKY [Resumed]
utterances.text: This territory was outside of our area of responsibility, outside of the area of responsibility of UN monitors. We were supposed to work only in the territory of Serbian Krajina. We had no jurisdiction in Bosnia, and we didn't make -- we didn't go there to patrol there at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I understand that, sir, but did you have any intelligence about the location of the 2nd Krajina Corps in Drvar?

utterances.speaker: ALEXANDER TCHERNETSKY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was in the team of observers. Let me put it this way: We collected information that was needed in accordance with our mandate. The information was provided to us by the headquarters. Now, what kind of information the headquarters received, I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So, without moving on, I will take that as a "No," sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let us move to D161. If we could just go into private session just briefly, Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Let's then also move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. Tchernetsky, I show you a document that was put together by the assistant commander for logistics for the army of Serb Krajina, a Mr. Bjelanovic, and I show you this page, and I want to take you to the fourth bullet point on this document and it begins with "Assistance." Now, you noted that, during your direct testimony, there were no military installation in Strmica, and this document notes that: "Assistance in the removal of RSK/MUP material from Strmica installation, everything that the army could used was allocated." Were you aware that there was a joint MUP/ARSK installation for supplies in Strmica?

utterances.speaker: ALEXANDER TCHERNETSKY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. As far as I know, and as far as we could observe, in Strmica, there were no military positions or firing positions at all. The closest military base of the Serbian army was much more to the south of Strmica. It was in the Golubici area. Golubici area is one of those areas that was closed off for our patrols. We were not given access to that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... so you were unaware of this joint installation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let me move on to page 3 of this document.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There was nothing in Strmica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let us move on to the next document -- page 3. I take you to about the middle of the page: "Due to not being able ..."

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay. Now, it notes in on the second bullet point, as you see: "Due to not being able to conduct work in the Strmica maintenance support company, the troops were ordered to redeploy units, assistance." Did you know there was a maintenance support company in Strmica?

utterances.speaker: ALEXANDER TCHERNETSKY [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Strmica itself, we did not see any presence of the Serbian troops.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Staying on that page, and moving down to the next entry on the 30th of July, of 1995, it notes that Mr. Bjelanovic, Colonel Bjelanovic: "I took part in making plans for attacking operations for Dinara 95." Did you know, sir, that the ARSK planned to attack the HV and began that plan in the late July of 1995?

utterances.speaker: ALEXANDER TCHERNETSKY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we did not know about such plans.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let us turn to the next page, and this is for the 31st of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Towards the top of the page before the entry of 8.02, on that last sentence: "On the Grahovo-Strmica road, the Ustasha laid mines on two bridges in order to prevent deployment of our troops and their replenishment with materiel." Now, were you aware that that, in fact, took place, that while the ARSK was trying to replenish troops on that road, that the HV had planted mines?

utterances.speaker: ALEXANDER TCHERNETSKY [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We were not informed about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let us turn to D62.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: D62, sir, is, again, another note from Colonel Bjelanovic dated 30th July 1995, Planning of Operation Dinara. Were you aware, sir, that they were moving troops beginning on the 31st of July to Strmica to begin this operation? Did you see that or did you observe any troop movements in that regard?

utterances.speaker: ALEXANDER TCHERNETSKY [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember now, with precision, whether it was 30th or 31st of July. It's been 13 years. But at any rate, all movement that was recorded by our patrols was included in the daily reports to the headquarters sector. So you should refer to our reports.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Based on your recollection, if it is in the sitrep or not, sir, is it your testimony that you don't recall any troop movements up into the Strmica area in late July of 1995 by the ARSK?

utterances.speaker: ALEXANDER TCHERNETSKY [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no major movement. I don't remember that we observed any major movement in that area. But, occasionally, we would come across some military vehicles or small columns that were, as a rule, moving in the direction of Golubic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And then from Golubic, if you move in the direction of Golubic, the next major town up is Strmica, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: ALEXANDER TCHERNETSKY [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Some seven or eight kilometres to the north of Golubic is where Strmica begins.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, likewise, just to cover one other issue in this page, in the indentation, it says, "7th Corps." It notes that there is an organi department. Do you see that, sir? Now, an organi is an M-77 rocket launcher, a 128-millimetre, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: ALEXANDER TCHERNETSKY [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, our team of monitors never reported on any movement of rocket launchers. We did not observe that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay, sir. Let me turn to the exact date that you there were. And if I may, one of the individuals that you went up there was an individual by the name of Peter Marti, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: ALEXANDER TCHERNETSKY [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you're referring to the visit to Strmica, then, yes. Peter Marti, Pavel Komper, Felix Anglada. They were with us they were members of our patrol team.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let me bring up a portion of Mr. Marti's diary, 1D23-0021.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, this has two notations to it: Saturday, the 29th of July, has the list of people on the team. You being one of them. 30th July, 1995 on Sunday: "Sundays are always a bother.
